STL hash specialization enabling triton::arch::register_e to be used as a key in unordered containers by reusing the uint64_t hash.

Abstract base class representing a processor architecture in Triton. It wraps a CpuInterface instance, exposes register/memory enumeration and concrete state manipulation, disassembly utilities, and architecture configuration (endianness, mode, etc.). Lifetimes: holds ownership of the underlying CPU via std::unique_ptr and a non-owning pointer to Callbacks. Destructor is not explicitly declared here; construction and destruction details beyond unique_ptr semantics are unknown from this header.

ARM AArch64 CPU model implementing Triton's CpuInterface and AArch64Specifications. Manages concrete register and memory state, disassembly context, and callback interactions. Provides queries for register classes and concrete state get/set APIs. Construction/destruction via standard constructors; no factory functions declared here. Owns internal memory map, register storage buffers, exclusive memory tag set, and a Capstone disassembly handle. Some behavior specifics (e.g., disassInit, copy) are defined in the implementation file.

AArch64Semantics defines the instruction semantics for the ARM AArch64 ISA within Triton. It implements SemanticsInterface and provides per-instruction semantic builders, flag computations, and control-flow handling. It holds pointers to the Architecture, SymbolicEngine, TaintEngine, an AST context, and maintains an exception status. Detailed construction/destruction policies are not documented in this header; lifetime of injected pointers is external/unknown.

objects.description: A global constant Instruction object representing the AArch64 NOP instruction (encoding 0xD503201F). Useful as a ready-made NOP for emission or testing. Note this is a const object, not a type; included here for completeness of definitions but it is not a user-defined type.

ARM 32-bit CPU model for Triton. Implements CpuInterface and Arm32Specifications, maintaining concrete register and memory state, disassembly contexts for ARM/Thumb, and utilities for condition handling and exclusive memory tagging. Provides API to query and set concrete values, disassemble instructions, and manage Thumb mode. Details like lifecycle and callback behavior follow Triton conventions; specific destruction/ownership rules beyond standard C++ are not documented here.

Concrete semantics builder for the 32-bit ARM ISA within Triton. Provides instruction-by-instruction semantic lifting, flag computation, taint/symbolic propagation, and control-flow modeling. Requires Architecture, SymbolicEngine, TaintEngine, and an AST context to operate. Destruction/ownership details are not stated; pointers to external engines are stored but not owned per this header.

Class providing ARM32 CPU specifications within Triton: register maps, and conversions from Capstone IDs to Triton enums and instruction IDs. Owns two maps from register IDs/names to Register specs. Construction requires an architecture_e. Destruction/ownership details are default/unspecified.
Two constant Instruction objects representing ARM32 NOP (ARM mode, 4 bytes) and Thumb NOP (2 bytes). Note: Instruction class itself is defined elsewhere; here only these constants are defined.

objects.description: Enumeration of all ARM32 and Thumb instruction identifiers used by Triton for this architecture. Values map logical instruction mnemonics to enum constants. No constructors; used as integral constants.

Concrete CPU model for the RISC-V 32-bit (RV32) architecture within Triton. Provides register files (GPR, FPU, PC, system registers), concrete memory storage, Capstone disassembly integration, and the CpuInterface/riscvSpecifications implementations for querying and setting concrete state, disassembly, and register classification.

Concrete RV64 CPU model for Triton. Provides register files, memory backing, disassembly handle, and implements CpuInterface over RISC-V 64-bit via riscvSpecifications. Manages concrete state (GPRs/FPRs/PC/system regs) and exposes getters/setters and query helpers.

Class implementing RISC‑V ISA semantics within Triton. Owns references to architecture, symbolic and taint engines, shared modes and AST context, and provides buildSemantics plus many per-instruction semantic builders. Lifetime and ownership of injected pointers are external; this class uses them to annotate and compute instruction semantics. Details of behaviors are defined in the source file; header provides interface only.

Class defining RISC-V (RV32/RV64) architecture specifications for Triton. It maps Capstone register/instruction/group IDs to Triton enums and provides special memory operand sizing. It maintains internal maps between register IDs and names to Triton Register objects. Construction requires an architecture_e to select RV32 vs RV64. Destruction/ownership details are not specified here.

objects.description: Enumeration of Triton RISC-V instruction opcodes, including base, atomic, floating point, and compressed instructions. Values start at 0 with ID_INS_INVALID and end with ID_INS_ENDING.

Represents a basic block within the Triton architecture module: a sequence of Instructions with single entry and exit. Manages a vector of triton::arch::Instruction and offers methods to add/remove instructions, query size, and obtain first/last instruction addresses. Construction, copy, assignment, and destruction are declared; definitions are external. Ownership of Instruction objects is by value within the vector.

Represents a contiguous bit-range (bit-vector slice) typically used to describe register or memory subranges by their high and low bit indices. Stores inclusive high/low indices as 32-bit unsigned integers and provides accessors, size computation, maximum representable value for the range width, and mutators. No destructor or special ownership semantics are declared; trivially movable/copyable by value.

Manager class that registers, removes, and invokes callbacks for Triton events (concrete memory/register get/set and symbolic simplification). Holds lists of functors for each kind and tracks definition state with atomics. Construction requires a Context reference managed externally. Thread-safety appears to be coordinated via atomic flags during callback processing.

Enumeration of callback kinds used by Triton’s callbacks subsystem. Values identify callback categories for concrete memory/register reads and writes, and symbolic simplification hooks. No additional methods or typedef aliases are defined in this header.

Main Triton context class. Aggregates and orchestrates architecture, IR builder, AST context, symbolic/solver/taint/lifting engines, modes, and callbacks. Provides high-level APIs for disassembly, processing, symbolic execution, taint analysis, solving, synthesis, and lifting. Construction/destruction are exported; engines are managed internally and may be nullptr until initialized. Users must set an architecture and call initEngines() before using dependent APIs.

std::string is a standard type; no custom type is defined here. This entry is invalid per instructions and should be ignored. Note: There are no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes defined in this header file.

Typedef alias for a 16-bit unsigned integer from <cstdint>. It is referenced as the return type of triton::sf::f32_to_f16, but not defined in this header. Per instructions, only types explicitly defined here should be documented; thus no custom types are defined in this header.

Abstract CPU interface for Triton architectures. It defines the required API for CPU implementations, covering register/memory querying and mutation, disassembly, endianness, mode flags (e.g., Thumb), and access to concrete state. This is a pure virtual class; instantiate concrete subclasses provided elsewhere.

Root exception class for Triton. Stores an error message and overrides std::exception::what(). Construct with a C-string or std::string; no special destruction required beyond default. Message is copied into an internal std::string.
Base exception class for all Triton engine-related errors. Inherits behavior from Exception; adds no new state.
Exception class for the symbolic engine and components thereof. No additional members.

Exception class for generic callback handling within Triton.
Exception class used specifically by Python callbacks. Always constructed with a fixed message indicating details are stored in Python state.

Represents an immediate operand in Triton’s architecture layer. Inherits bit-width/bitvector behavior from BitsVector and ARM-specific operand properties from arm::ArmOperandProperties. Stores the immediate’s value (uint64) and exposes constructors for integral and double sources with size and endianness, accessors for value/size, and standard comparison/streaming helpers (as free operators). Destruction/ownership details are standard C++ object semantics; no custom destructor is declared here. Some behavioral details depend on the base classes, which are defined elsewhere.

Represents a decoded and semantically analyzed instruction within Triton’s architecture layer. It stores metadata (architecture, address, size, type, disassembly, prefixes/conditions), decoded operands, and semantic side-effects (reads/writes of memory and registers, immediates, undefined regs), plus symbolic expressions attached to the instruction. Provides rich query and mutation APIs to build, analyze, and update instruction state during disassembly and symbolic execution. Construction/destruction handled via exported constructors/destructor; no special ownership beyond standard C++ semantics is required.

IR builder for Triton architectures. It constructs intermediate representation (semantics) for single instructions and basic blocks using architecture, modes, AST context, symbolic engine, and taint engine. Owns no resources by value; holds raw pointers/references to external subsystems. Construction requires valid subsystem pointers/handles; destruction does not delete external subsystems (lifetime managed elsewhere). Methods provide pre/post hooks and semantic builders. Unknown internal algorithms; semantically ties to platform-specific SemanticsInterface implementations (AArch64, ARM32, x86, RISC-V).

LiftingEngine is a concrete lifter that aggregates multiple lifting backends (SMT, DOT, optionally LLVM, and Python) by inheriting from their lifter base classes. It initializes each backend with a shared AST context and a symbolic engine to enable lifting symbolic expressions into different target representations. Destructor, copy/move semantics, and other methods are not declared in this header; only the constructor is provided inline.

A lifter utility that converts Triton ASTs and symbolic expressions into Graphviz DOT representation. It holds references to the AST context and a SymbolicEngine, tracks nodes/edges, and emits DOT to a provided std::ostream. Construction requires an AST context and a pointer to the symbolic engine. Destruction/ownership details are not specified; the class does not own external pointers by contract implied from member types.

Class that lifts Triton symbolic expressions into Python code. It holds an AST context and a pointer to the symbolic engine, and can emit helper functions required by generated Python (e.g., ror, rol, sx, forall). Construction requires an AST context and a symbolic engine pointer. Destruction/ownership semantics are not specified here; the class does not appear to own the symbolic engine (raw pointer).

Class that lifts Triton symbolic expressions into SMT text form. Holds an AST context (for node handling) and a pointer to the symbolic engine. Provides a constructor to bind these dependencies and a liftToSMT method to emit SMT for a given symbolic expression, optionally wrapping it in an assert and including instruction comments. The requiredFunctions helper outputs any prerequisite SMT function definitions (e.g., bswap). No destruction semantics are specified here; ownership of the AST context handle and the symbolic engine pointer is not clarified in this header.

Represents a memory operand/access in Triton’s architecture layer. Inherits from BitsVector to carry bit-size/bitvector semantics. Encapsulates concrete address, optional PC-relative offset, LEA-style addressing components (segment, base, index, displacement, scale), and an AST node describing the effective address. Provides getters/setters, comparison and overlap checks. Construction is via default, address+size, or copy constructors. Lifetime is standard C++ stack/heap; no special destruction is declared in this header.

A configurable container class that tracks which Triton execution/analysis modes are enabled. Internally stores a set of triton::modes::mode_e values and provides APIs to query, enable/disable specific modes, and clear all modes. Construction and copy/assignment are explicitly declared; destruction is implicit. Detailed semantics of individual modes depend on triton::modes::mode_e (declared elsewhere).

objects.definition: using SharedModes = std::shared_ptr<triton::modes::Modes>;
objects.description: Alias for a shared-ownership smart pointer to Modes, enabling shared lifetime management of a Modes instance across components.

Enumeration of Triton engine modes controlling symbolic execution, AST optimizations, memory modeling, taint behavior, and path constraint tracking. Values indicate togglable engine features. The std::hash specialization enables use in unordered containers.

Class that wraps a Triton architecture operand, storing exactly one of: Immediate, MemoryAccess, or Register, along with its operand_e type tag. Provides constructors for each operand kind, accessors/mutators, size/bit-range queries, and comparison operators. Useful for handling heterogeneous operands uniformly. Ownership: it stores copies of the underlying operand objects. Destruction/cleanup is trivial as there are no dynamic allocations visible here. Details about exact semantics of size/high/low depend on Immediate/MemoryAccess/Register types and operand_e, which are defined elsewhere.

Entry for the oracle table used during constant synthesis. Holds the AST operator node and the position of the constant operand within the expression. Construction requires providing the constant position (e.g., 0 or 1) and the AST node representing the operator. Destruction is trivial; members are value/RAII types.

Oracle entry for unary operator synthesis. Captures the bit-size of the operation domain, an input value x, and the resulting value r = op(x). Construction requires the bit width, input, and result. Destruction is trivial.
Oracle entry for binary operator synthesis. Stores bit-size, inputs x and y, and result r = x <op> y. Construction requires the bit width, both operands, and the result. Destruction is trivial.

Represents a single path constraint in Triton’s symbolic execution engine. Internally stores a sequence of branch alternatives as tuples of (taken flag, source address, destination address, predicate AST). Also records an optional thread id and an arbitrary comment. Provides APIs to append branch entries and query the taken branch, its predicate, source address, multiplicity, thread id, and comment. Construction and destruction are managed normally; no explicit ownership semantics to other types are declared here.

PathManager collects and manages the sequence of symbolic path constraints produced during execution. It owns a vector of PathConstraint elements and exposes methods to push/pop/clear constraints, query subsets, compute the current path predicate, and derive predicates to reach an address. Construction requires SharedModes and SharedAstContext objects that configure global modes and the AST context. Detailed semantics of PathConstraint and AST nodes are defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: class CpuInterface;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the CpuInterface class within triton::arch. Only a declaration is present in this header; its interface and ownership semantics are unknown here.

Represents a register operand in Triton’s architecture layer. Inherits bit-range handling from BitsVector and architecture-specific ARM operand properties from arm::ArmOperandProperties. Holds register name, id, parent id (covering register), and a mutability flag (e.g., XZR immutable). Public API includes constructors (default, explicit spec, from CpuInterface+id, copy), queries (name, id, parent, size, type, mutability), overlap testing, comparisons, and assignment. Details of construction behavior and validation depend on implementations not present in this header.

Abstract interface in triton::arch that all ISA semantics implementations must derive from. It provides a virtual destructor and a pure-virtual buildSemantics method that fills/builds the semantics for a given Instruction and returns an exception_e status (NO_FAULT on success). No ownership semantics or additional state are defined here.

Helper class providing pre-instantiated triton::arch::Register members for many CPU architectures (x86/x86_64, AArch64, ARM32, RISC-V). It allows quick, name-based access to register objects via fields like x86_rax, aarch64_x0, arm32_r0, riscv_x1, etc., populated by init(architecture_e). clear() resets all to default Register instances. The actual member list is generated by including architecture-specific spec files via macros.

Concrete engine class in triton::engines::solver that wraps a backend SMT solver. It manages the solver kind (solver_e) and owns a SolverInterface instance via unique_ptr. Provides methods to set a predefined or custom solver, query satisfiability, fetch one or multiple models, and configure timeout and memory limits. Destruction and lifecycle are managed by the class; callers should not delete the internal solver pointer. Exact construction details of backends are defined in the implementation, not in this header.

Enumeration of supported SMT solver backends within Triton. Values may be conditionally compiled based on available interfaces (e.g., Z3 or Bitwuzla). Used to select a concrete solver implementation; not an instantiable object.
Enumeration describing the result status of a solver query: satisfiable, unsatisfiable, timeout, out-of-memory, or unknown. Used as return/status codes by solver operations.

Abstract interface for Triton solver backends. Provides pure virtual methods to query satisfiability, obtain one or multiple models from an AST constraint, retrieve the solver name, and configure timeout and memory limits. This header only declares the interface; concrete implementations are defined elsewhere.

Represents a solved constraint model: pairs a symbolic variable with the concrete value assigned by a solver. Holds a SharedSymbolicVariable handle and the corresponding 512-bit value. Provides accessors for variable id, size, value, and the variable itself, plus comparison and stream output. Construction details (resource ownership, lifetime of SharedSymbolicVariable) are not fully documented here and depend on the symbolic subsystem.

Primary symbolic execution engine for Triton. Manages creation, storage, and manipulation of symbolic expressions and variables, ties them to architecture state (registers/memory), and provides AST builders for operands. Inherits from SymbolicSimplification and PathManager. Construction requires architecture, modes, AST context, and optional callbacks. Lifetime and ownership of architecture/callbacks are external; engine stores raw pointers to them.

Enumeration of symbolic expression kinds within triton::engines::symbolic. Values distinguish whether an expression originates from memory, a register, or is marked volatile. Used to classify/dispatch handling of expressions. No extra constraints are documented here.

Enumeration of symbolic variable categories within triton::engines::symbolic. Indicates whether a variable corresponds to memory, a register, or is undefined. Useful for tagging and validation of symbolic variables.

Symbolic expression object used by Triton’s symbolic engine. Encapsulates an AST node describing the semantics, bookkeeping (id, type, taint, address, disassembly), and optional origin (register or memory) of the assignment that produced the expression. Provides formatted renderers, accessors/mutators, and copy semantics. Details about construction semantics and lifetime beyond the provided interface are not documented in this header.

objects.definition: using SharedSymbolicExpression = std::shared_ptr<triton::engines::symbolic::SymbolicExpression>;
objects.description: Alias for a shared_ptr managing a SymbolicExpression instance. Use to share ownership across components.

objects.definition: using WeakSymbolicExpression = std::weak_ptr<triton::engines::symbolic::SymbolicExpression>;
objects.description: Alias for a weak_ptr observing a SymbolicExpression without affecting its lifetime.

Class providing symbolic simplification facilities within Triton’s symbolic execution engine. It holds an Architecture context and optional Callbacks to drive transformations. Public API includes simplifying AST nodes and performing dead-store elimination on a BasicBlock. Construction requires an Architecture pointer; Callbacks is optional. Copy and assignment are supported. Destruction behavior is not specified here; ownership of the Architecture/Callbacks pointers is unknown and likely not owned by this class.

Concrete class representing a symbolic variable used by Triton’s symbolic execution engine. It encapsulates metadata such as type (register or memory), alias, comment, canonical name, unique id, origin (register id or memory address), and bit-size. Provides accessor and mutator methods for alias/comment. Construction requires specifying type, origin, id, size, and an alias. Copy and assignment are supported. Details about lifetime management are typical C++: objects can be owned via std::shared_ptr and std::weak_ptr aliases provided in this header.

objects.definition: using SharedSymbolicVariable = std::shared_ptr<triton::engines::symbolic::SymbolicVariable>;
objects.description: Type alias for a shared_ptr managing a SymbolicVariable instance. Use to share ownership of a SymbolicVariable.

objects.definition: using WeakSymbolicVariable = std::weak_ptr<triton::engines::symbolic::SymbolicVariable>;
objects.description: Type alias for a weak_ptr referencing a SymbolicVariable managed elsewhere. Use to observe without extending lifetime.

Engine result container for the Triton synthesis subsystem. It records whether synthesis succeeded, the input AST node provided, the output AST node (either the synthesized node on success or the same as input on failure), and the elapsed time in milliseconds. Construction/destruction semantics are standard C++ value semantics; copying and assignment are supported. No ownership of AST nodes beyond the semantics of triton::ast::SharedAbstractNode (a shared pointer-like handle defined elsewhere) is implied. Details like default field values and exception guarantees are not present in this header.

Synthesis engine that attempts to rewrite an AST node into a simpler or equivalent expression by introducing temporary symbolic variables and matching against oracle tables. It holds an internal solver, a pointer to the symbolic engine, and maps to track subexpression symbolization and synthesized replacements. Construction requires a SymbolicEngine*. Details of internal synthesis strategies are private to the class.

Taint analysis engine for Triton. Tracks tainted memory addresses and registers and provides APIs to taint, untaint, and propagate taint via union and assignment semantics across operands. It depends on modes, the symbolic engine, and the CPU interface, which are injected at construction. Internals store tainted memory addresses and an over-approximated set of tainted registers.

x8664Cpu models the 64-bit x86 CPU for Triton. It derives from CpuInterface and x86Specifications and encapsulates register state, concrete memory, and disassembly/utility methods. It stores concrete values for general-purpose, SIMD/FPU, control, debug, and system registers, and exposes APIs to query/modify register and memory state and to disassemble instructions. Construction/destruction details are not fully visible here; TRITON_EXPORT indicates out-of-line definitions.

x86Cpu models a 32-bit x86 CPU for Triton. It implements CpuInterface and x86Specifications, owns concrete state storage for registers, memory, and some system registers, and provides APIs to query, mutate, and disassemble instructions for the architecture. Construction requires or optionally accepts a Callbacks pointer; it manages an internal disassembler handle. Destruction semantics are not detailed here; follow Triton’s lifecycle rules. Details like disassembler backend setup are internal.

Class implementing x86 ISA semantics within Triton. Provides semantic builders for a wide range of x86 instructions and flag computations. Holds references to Architecture, SymbolicEngine, TaintEngine, shared Modes, AST context, and maintains last exception status. Construct with provided Triton subsystems; primary API is buildSemantics(Instruction&).

Class providing x86/x86_64 architectural specifications and mappings between external (Capstone) identifiers and Triton enums. Holds register specification maps. Construction requires an architecture_e to select x86 or x86_64 specifics.

objects.description: Enumeration of Triton’s x86/x86_64 instruction identifiers. Values cover legacy, SSE/AVX, BMI, SHA, SGX, and virtualization instructions. Used as canonical IDs within Triton.

functions.name: triton::arch::Architecture::Architecture
functions.description: Constructs an Architecture wrapper around a concrete CPU backend and optional callbacks dispatcher. Pass a Callbacks instance to receive architecture events, or nullptr to disable callbacks.
requirements: callbacks may be nullptr (default)
If non-null, callbacks must outlive any operations that invoke them through this Architecture instance (inferred)

functions.name: triton::arch::Architecture::isFlag
functions.description: Checks if the given register ID corresponds to a flag register in the current architecture.
requirements: Architecture must be set/initialized before use to have a valid register set (inferred)

functions.name: triton::arch::Architecture::isRegister
functions.description: Checks if the given register ID corresponds to a general register (non-flag) in the current architecture.
requirements: Architecture must be set/initialized before use (inferred)

functions.name: triton::arch::Architecture::isRegisterValid
functions.description: Checks if the given register ID is a valid register or flag in the current architecture.
requirements: Architecture must be set/initialized before use (inferred)

functions.name: triton::arch::Architecture::isValid
functions.description: Returns true if the Architecture object is configured with a supported CPU/architecture.
requirements: None explicitly; typically requires setArchitecture() to have been called (inferred)

functions.name: triton::arch::Architecture::isThumb
functions.description: Returns true if the current execution mode is Thumb. Only valid for Arm32.
requirements: Only call for Arm32 architectures; behavior is only valid for Arm32 as documented

functions.name: triton::arch::Architecture::setThumb
functions.description: Sets the CPU execution mode to or from Thumb. Only valid for Arm32.
requirements: Only call for Arm32 architectures; setting Thumb is only valid for Arm32 as documented

functions.name: triton::arch::Architecture::isMemoryExclusive
functions.description: Returns true if the specified memory access is tagged as exclusive. Only valid for Arm32 and AArch64.
requirements: Only call for Arm32 or AArch64 architectures as documented
mem must describe a valid memory access in the current architecture (inferred)

functions.name: triton::arch::Architecture::setMemoryExclusiveTag
functions.description: Sets or clears the exclusive access tag on the specified memory location. Only valid for Arm32 and AArch64.
requirements: Only call for Arm32 or AArch64 architectures as documented
mem must describe a valid memory access in the current architecture (inferred)

functions.name: triton::ComparableFunctor::ComparableFunctor
functions.description: Constructor that wraps an existing std::function and associates an identifier pointer used for equality comparison. Use this when you have a std::function matching Signature and you want ComparableFunctor instances created with the same ID to compare equal.
requirements: Signature must denote a valid callable signature compatible with the std::function passed as F.
F must be callable according to Signature at the call sites used with operator().
ID may be any pointer; equality and inequality operators use the raw pointer value for comparison.
No default constructor exists; instances must be constructed with a callable.

functions.name: triton::ComparableFunctor::operator()
functions.signature:
template <class Signature>
template <class apiType>
auto triton::ComparableFunctor<Signature>::operator()(apiType& api) const -> decltype(F_(api))
functions.description: Invokes the wrapped callable with a single api argument, forwarding to the underlying std::function. The return type is deduced from the wrapped callable.
requirements: The wrapped callable F_ must be invocable with a single argument of type apiType&.
api must be a valid lvalue matching what the underlying callable expects.
Any exceptions thrown by the wrapped callable propagate to the caller.

functions.name: triton::ComparableFunctor::operator()
functions.signature:
template <class Signature>
template <class apiType, class paramType>
auto triton::ComparableFunctor<Signature>::operator()(apiType& api, paramType& param) const -> decltype(F_(api, param))
functions.description: Invokes the wrapped callable with two lvalue reference arguments, forwarding to the underlying std::function. The return type is deduced from the wrapped callable.
requirements: The wrapped callable F_ must be invocable with arguments of types apiType& and paramType&.
api and param must be valid lvalues matching what the underlying callable expects.
Any exceptions thrown by the wrapped callable propagate to the caller.

functions.name: triton::ComparableFunctor::operator()
functions.signature:
template <class Signature>
template <class apiType, class paramType1, class paramType2>
auto triton::ComparableFunctor<Signature>::operator()(apiType& api, paramType1& param1, paramType2& param2) const -> decltype(F_(api, param1, param2))
functions.description: Invokes the wrapped callable with three lvalue reference arguments, forwarding to the underlying std::function. This non-variadic overload exists for compiler compatibility. The return type is deduced from the wrapped callable.
requirements: The wrapped callable F_ must be invocable with arguments of types apiType&, paramType1&, and paramType2&.
api, param1, and param2 must be valid lvalues matching what the underlying callable expects.
Any exceptions thrown by the wrapped callable propagate to the caller.

functions.name: triton::ComparableFunctor::operator==
functions.signature:
template <class Signature>
template <class T>
bool triton::ComparableFunctor<Signature>::operator==(const triton::ComparableFunctor<T>& O) const
functions.description: Compares two ComparableFunctor instances for equality based solely on their stored identifier pointer (ID_). Two functors compare equal if their ID_ pointers are the same, regardless of callable content or Signature.
requirements: Equality depends only on the ID_ values provided/derived at construction; callers must ensure they pass the same ID pointer to represent logical equality (e.g., reuse the same ID when wrapping equivalent callables).
O may be any ComparableFunctor with any Signature parameter; only IDs are compared.

functions.name: triton::ComparableFunctor::operator!=
functions.signature:
template <class Signature>
template <class T>
bool triton::ComparableFunctor<Signature>::operator!=(const triton::ComparableFunctor<T>& O) const
functions.description: Inequality operator; returns the negation of operator== by comparing the stored identifier pointers (ID_).
requirements: Inequality depends only on the ID_ values; if IDs differ, functors are considered not equal.
O may be any ComparableFunctor with any Signature parameter; only IDs are compared.

functions.name: triton::sf::f32_to_f16
functions.description: Converts a 32-bit IEEE-754 floating-point value (float) to its 16-bit IEEE-754 binary16 (half-precision) encoding and returns the raw 16-bit bit pattern as a uint16_t. Use this to store or transmit half-precision values without a native half type. Information loss may occur due to reduced precision/range. Handling of special values (NaN, infinities, subnormals) follows IEEE-754, but specific rounding mode and NaN payload propagation are not specified in this header.
requirements: Argument value: any 32-bit float is accepted, including finite values, NaN, and infinities (per the function’s stated IEEE-754 behavior).
No initialization or prior setup is required to call this function.
The return value is a raw IEEE-754 binary16 bit pattern; callers must not treat it as a float without appropriate conversion.
Do not rely on a specific rounding mode or NaN payload-preservation behavior; these details are not specified here.

functions.name: triton::arch::IrBuilder::IrBuilder
functions.signature: triton::arch::IrBuilder::IrBuilder(triton::arch::Architecture* architecture, const triton::modes::SharedModes& modes, const triton::ast::SharedAstContext& astCtxt, triton::engines::symbolic::SymbolicEngine* symbolicEngine, triton::engines::taint::TaintEngine* taintEngine)
functions.description: Constructs an IR builder wired to the given architecture, modes, AST context, symbolic engine, and taint engine. Intended to be used to build instruction/block semantics for the configured architecture.
requirements: architecture must be a valid, non-null pointer and must remain alive for the lifetime of the IrBuilder (stored as a raw pointer).
symbolicEngine must be a valid, non-null pointer and must remain alive for the lifetime of the IrBuilder (stored as a raw pointer).
taintEngine must be a valid, non-null pointer and must remain alive for the lifetime of the IrBuilder (stored as a raw pointer).
modes must reference a valid SharedModes object; it is held by value (shared) and must refer to a properly initialized modes instance.
astCtxt must reference a valid SharedAstContext; it must be initialized and compatible with the symbolic engine usage.
All provided components should be configured for the same target architecture to avoid inconsistent semantics generation.

functions.name: triton::arch::IrBuilder::~IrBuilder
functions.description: Destructor for the IR builder. Cleans up any resources owned by the builder. Does not manage the lifetime of external components passed to the constructor (raw pointers).
requirements: Do not destroy or invalidate the Architecture, SymbolicEngine, or TaintEngine objects before destroying the IrBuilder, as the builder may reference them during its lifetime.

functions.name: triton::arch::IrBuilder::buildSemantics
functions.description: Builds the semantics (IR/AST, symbolic and taint effects) of a single instruction. Returns triton::arch::NO_FAULT on success; otherwise returns an architecture-specific exception code.
requirements: inst must be a valid Instruction object initialized/decoded for the same architecture as this IrBuilder.
Caller must check the returned triton::arch::exception_e; success is indicated by triton::arch::NO_FAULT.
inst will be modified to attach semantic information; caller should not assume inst remains unchanged.
If using pre/post hooks manually, ensure preIrInit(inst) is called before and postIrInit(inst) after custom building steps; otherwise, use this function which performs a full build sequence.

functions.name: triton::arch::IrBuilder::buildSemantics
functions.description: Builds the semantics for all instructions in the given basic block, in order. Returns triton::arch::NO_FAULT on success; otherwise returns an architecture-specific exception code.
requirements: block must contain valid, initialized instructions for the same architecture as this IrBuilder.
Caller must check the returned triton::arch::exception_e; success is indicated by triton::arch::NO_FAULT.
Instructions within block may be modified to attach semantic information; caller should not assume they remain unchanged.
Control-flow or fault conditions within the block may stop processing early if a non-NO_FAULT is encountered (behavior depends on implementation; exact details not specified).

functions.name: triton::arch::IrBuilder::preIrInit
functions.description: Performs all preparatory steps required before building the semantics of an instruction (e.g., clearing prior state, preparing engines). Intended to be called before custom or manual semantic construction.
requirements: inst must be a valid Instruction associated with this builder’s architecture.
Call before building semantics for inst when not using the high-level buildSemantics API.
After calling preIrInit, the caller is expected to either call buildSemantics or complete a corresponding postIrInit to finalize state.

functions.name: triton::arch::IrBuilder::postIrInit
functions.description: Performs all finalization steps after building the semantics of an instruction (e.g., recording generated expressions, cleanup). Intended to be called after custom or manual semantic construction.
requirements: inst must be a valid Instruction associated with this builder’s architecture.
Call after semantics for inst have been built when not using the high-level buildSemantics API.
Should typically be paired with a preceding preIrInit(inst) call to ensure proper initialization/finalization sequence.

functions.name: triton::engines::lifters::LiftingToDot::LiftingToDot
functions.description: Constructs a lifter that emits Graphviz DOT representations of Triton ASTs and symbolic expressions. Use this to visualize ASTs/expressions managed by the provided AST context and symbolic engine. The instance stores the AST context and a pointer to the symbolic engine for resolving references while lifting.
requirements: astCtxt must be an initialized AST context object suitable for the nodes/expressions to be lifted (inferred from purpose and parameter type).
symbolic must be a valid, non-null pointer to a triton::engines::symbolic::SymbolicEngine (inferred from internal storage and lifter purpose).
The symbolic engine pointer must remain valid for all subsequent calls to lift methods on this LiftingToDot instance (inferred from storage of a raw pointer).

functions.name: triton::engines::lifters::LiftingToDot::liftToDot
functions.description: Writes a Graphviz DOT representation of the given Triton AST node and all its referenced information to the provided output stream. Use this to visualize a specific AST subtree. Returns the same stream to allow chaining.
requirements: stream must be a valid, writable std::ostream; it will be written to and returned (inferred from signature and typical ostream usage).
node must be a valid (non-null) SharedAbstractNode managed by the AST context associated with this LiftingToDot (inferred from purpose and parameter type).
The LiftingToDot instance must have been constructed with a compatible AST context and a valid symbolic engine if symbolic references are resolved during lifting (inferred from class design).

functions.name: triton::engines::lifters::LiftingToDot::liftToDot
functions.description: Writes a Graphviz DOT representation of the given symbolic expression and any referenced ASTs/expressions to the provided output stream. Use this to visualize a symbolic expression’s dependency graph. Returns the same stream to allow chaining.
requirements: stream must be a valid, writable std::ostream; it will be written to and returned (inferred from signature and typical ostream usage).
expr must be a valid (non-null) SharedSymbolicExpression originating from the symbolic engine associated with this LiftingToDot (inferred from purpose and parameter type).
The LiftingToDot instance must have been constructed with a valid symbolic engine that remains alive while this function executes (inferred from storage of a raw pointer).

functions.name: triton::engines::lifters::LiftingToPython::LiftingToPython
functions.description: Constructor. Initializes a LiftingToPython instance with an AST context and a pointer to the symbolic engine. Use this to prepare a lifter that can emit Python code for Triton symbolic expressions built from the provided AST context/symbolic engine.
requirements: astCtxt must be a valid, initialized AST context object (by reference).
symbolic must be a valid, non-null pointer to a triton::engines::symbolic::SymbolicEngine instance.

The provided symbolic engine and AST context are expected to remain valid for the duration of any lift operations performed by this LiftingToPython instance (lifetime/ownership management is the caller’s responsibility).

functions.name: triton::engines::lifters::LiftingToPython::liftToPython
functions.signature: std::ostream& triton::engines::lifters::LiftingToPython::liftToPython(std::ostream& stream, const triton::engines::symbolic::SharedSymbolicExpression& expr, bool icomment=false)
functions.description: Lifts a symbolic expression and all of its referenced expressions to a Python representation and writes it to the provided output stream. When icomment is true, instruction assembly is included in comments alongside the emitted code. Returns the same output stream to allow chaining.
requirements: stream must be a valid std::ostream open for writing; it must outlive the call.
expr must be a valid, non-null SharedSymbolicExpression managed by Triton’s symbolic engine.
The expression’s AST/context should be compatible with the AST context and symbolic engine that this LiftingToPython instance was constructed with (inferred from design).
Call only after constructing LiftingToPython with appropriate astCtxt and symbolic engine. The LiftingToPython object must remain alive for the duration of the call.
Caller should check the state of the returned stream to detect I/O errors.

functions.name: triton::engines::lifters::LiftingToSMT::LiftingToSMT
functions.description: Constructs a lifter that converts Triton symbolic expressions to SMT. The instance keeps a reference to the AST context and a pointer to the symbolic engine, which it uses to resolve and emit expressions in SMT-LIB form. Typical usage: create once with the process-wide AST context and the symbolic engine instance, then call liftToSMT for expressions you want to serialize.
requirements: astCtxt must be a valid AST context object usable for building/handling AST nodes.
symbolic must be a non-null pointer to a live triton::engines::symbolic::SymbolicEngine instance for as long as the LiftingToSMT object uses it.
No ownership transfer is implied by the constructor; the caller remains responsible for managing the lifetime of the symbolic engine pointer.

functions.name: triton::engines::lifters::LiftingToSMT::liftToSMT
functions.signature: std::ostream& triton::engines::lifters::LiftingToSMT::liftToSMT(std::ostream& stream, const triton::engines::symbolic::SharedSymbolicExpression& expr, bool assert_ = false, bool icomment = false)
functions.description: Lifts a symbolic expression and all of its referenced expressions to SMT format and writes the result to the provided stream. If assert_ is true, the emitted SMT wraps the expression in an (assert <expr>) form. If icomment is true, instruction assembly text is included in comments in the output. Returns the same stream to allow chaining.
requirements: stream must be a valid, writable std::ostream that remains alive for the duration of the call.
expr must be a valid (non-null) triton::engines::symbolic::SharedSymbolicExpression.
The expression should be compatible with the AST context and symbolic engine provided at construction (i.e., created by the same Triton engine/context).
assert_ and icomment can be set independently to control assertion wrapping and inclusion of instruction comments in the SMT output.

functions.name: triton::engines::synthesis::OpEncoding::OpEncoding
functions.signature: template<std::size_t N> triton::engines::synthesis::OpEncoding<N>::OpEncoding(std::array<triton::ast::ast_e, N> ops, std::array<triton::uint8, N + 1> vars)
functions.description: Constructs an encoding that captures the operator ordering and variable selection for a composed expression. ops lists N AST operator kinds (e.g., BVADD, BVMUL), and vars lists the sequence of variable indices used at each step (N+1 entries). Used as a key or descriptor for oracle data associated with a particular expression shape.
requirements: Template parameter N must match the sizes of the provided arrays (ops has length N, vars has length N+1).
ops elements must be valid triton::ast::ast_e operator identifiers for the intended expression.
vars elements are indices that select variables as indicated by examples; callers should supply indices consistent with the expression’s variables.

functions.name: triton::engines::synthesis::operator<
functions.signature: template<std::size_t N> bool triton::engines::synthesis::operator<(const triton::engines::synthesis::OpEncoding<N>& obj1, const triton::engines::synthesis::OpEncoding<N>& obj2)
functions.description: Provides a strict-weak ordering for OpEncoding objects by comparing their addresses. This is intended to allow OpEncoding to be used as a key in associative containers, but note it orders by object identity, not by content.
requirements: obj1 and obj2 must be valid references to live OpEncoding objects for the duration of the comparison.

Ordering is based on object addresses; it is not a semantic/content-based ordering. Using this as a key comparator implies that only pointer identity is considered, and distinct copies of equal encodings will not compare equal.

functions.description: Performs program synthesis over the given AST node. When constant is true, attempts constant synthesis; when opaque is true, attempts opaque-constant synthesis; when subexpr is true, it analyzes and may synthesize child subexpressions. Typical usage: provide a valid AST node from the Triton AST context, optionally choose synthesis modes via flags, and examine the returned SynthesisResult for the outcome.

The Synthesizer instance must have been constructed with a valid SymbolicEngine prior to calling synthesize (inferred from class design).

The meaning of combinations of constant and opaque is per comments: constant enables constant synthesis; opaque enables opaque constant synthesis; callers should set flags consistently; unspecified combinations beyond these modes are allowed but semantics beyond the comment are unknown.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getProgramCounter
functions.description: Returns the Register descriptor for the program counter (EIP) in the x86 model.
requirements: No parameters.
Returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the CPU instance.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getRegister
functions.description: Returns the Register descriptor associated with the given register id.
requirements: id must be a valid register id for this architecture; behavior for invalid ids is unspecified (may throw or assert depending on build).

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getRegister
functions.description: Looks up and returns the Register descriptor by its name (e.g., "eax").
requirements: name must match a known register name for this architecture; matching rules (case sensitivity) are unspecified.
Behavior when the name is not found is unspecified (may throw or assert depending on build).

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getStackPointer
functions.description: Returns the Register descriptor for the stack pointer (ESP) in the x86 model.
requirements: No parameters.
Returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the CPU instance.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getParentRegisters
functions.description: Returns a set of pointers to all parent (top-level) registers in the x86 model (e.g., EAX, EBX, ...).
requirements: Returned pointers are valid as long as the CPU instance exists.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getConcreteMemoryAreaValue
functions.signature: std::vector<triton::uint8> triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getConcreteMemoryAreaValue(triton::uint64 baseAddr, triton::usize size, bool execCallbacks = true) const
functions.description: Reads a contiguous area of concrete memory bytes starting at baseAddr for the given size and returns them as a vector. If execCallbacks is true, registered callbacks may be invoked on reads.
requirements: size specifies the number of bytes to read; behavior for size == 0 is to return an empty vector (typical), though not explicitly documented.
Addresses not present in the concrete memory map are treated as undefined; behavior when reading undefined memory may involve callbacks or default values per library configuration.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getEndianness
functions.description: Returns the endianness of the x86 CPU model (x86 is little-endian).
requirements: No parameters.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::numberOfRegisters
functions.description: Returns the total number of registers modeled by this x86 CPU instance.
requirements: No parameters.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::gprBitSize
functions.description: Returns the bit size of general-purpose registers in this model (32 for x86).
requirements: No parameters.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::gprSize
functions.description: Returns the byte size of general-purpose registers in this model (4 for x86).
requirements: No parameters.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getConcreteMemoryValue
functions.signature: triton::uint512 triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getConcreteMemoryValue(const triton::arch::MemoryAccess& mem, bool execCallbacks = true) const
functions.description: Reads the concrete value for the specified memory access region and returns it as a uint512 container wide enough to hold the requested size. If execCallbacks is true, registered callbacks may be invoked on reads.
requirements: mem must specify a valid address and size (>0).
The size encoded in mem determines how many bits of the returned uint512 are meaningful.
Reading undefined memory may invoke callbacks or return default/undefined values per configuration.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getConcreteMemoryValue
functions.signature: triton::uint8 triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getConcreteMemoryValue(triton::uint64 addr, bool execCallbacks = true) const
functions.description: Reads a single byte of concrete memory at the specified address. If execCallbacks is true, registered callbacks may be invoked on the read.
requirements: No explicit alignment requirements; reads one byte at addr.
Reading an undefined address may invoke callbacks or return default/undefined values per configuration.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getConcreteRegisterValue
functions.signature: triton::uint512 triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::getConcreteRegisterValue(const triton::arch::Register& reg, bool execCallbacks = true) const
functions.description: Returns the current concrete value of the specified register as a uint512 container wide enough to hold the register size. If execCallbacks is true, registered callbacks may be invoked on reads.
requirements: reg must be a valid Register from this CPU model.
Register size determines how many bits of the returned uint512 are meaningful.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::clear
functions.description: Clears the CPU state, resetting concrete register values and the concrete memory map to their default/empty state.
requirements: No parameters.
All previously obtained references into internal containers may become invalid after clear.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::disassembly
functions.description: Disassembles the provided instruction buffer according to the x86 (32-bit) architecture and populates the Instruction object with decoding results using the configured disassembler context.
requirements: inst must contain sufficient bytes and context (address/size) for disassembly; exact requirements depend on the Instruction type.
May use internal callbacks and disassembler handle; behavior if disassembler is uninitialized is unspecified.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setConcreteMemoryAreaValue
functions.signature: void triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setConcreteMemoryAreaValue(triton::uint64 baseAddr, const std::vector<triton::uint8>& values, bool execCallbacks = true)
functions.description: Writes a contiguous area of concrete memory starting at baseAddr with the provided byte vector. If execCallbacks is true, registered callbacks may be invoked on writes.
requirements: values.size() defines the number of bytes written; writing zero bytes is a no-op.
baseAddr + values.size() may overlap existing defined memory; it will overwrite those bytes.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setConcreteMemoryAreaValue
functions.signature: void triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setConcreteMemoryAreaValue(triton::uint64 baseAddr, const void* area, triton::usize size, bool execCallbacks = true)
functions.description: Writes a contiguous area of concrete memory from a raw buffer starting at baseAddr for size bytes. If execCallbacks is true, registered callbacks may be invoked on writes.
requirements: area must point to at least size bytes of readable memory when size > 0.
size is the number of bytes to write; size == 0 performs no write.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setConcreteMemoryValue
functions.signature: void triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setConcreteMemoryValue(const triton::arch::MemoryAccess& mem, const triton::uint512& value, bool execCallbacks = true)
functions.description: Writes the concrete value for the specified memory access region. The number of bits written is defined by mem.size; only the corresponding low bits of value are used. If execCallbacks is true, registered callbacks may be invoked on writes.
requirements: mem must specify a valid address and size (>0).
value must contain at least mem.size bits of data; higher bits are ignored.
Writes may overlap existing memory definitions and overwrite them.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setConcreteMemoryValue
functions.signature: void triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setConcreteMemoryValue(triton::uint64 addr, triton::uint8 value, bool execCallbacks = true)
functions.description: Writes a single concrete byte to the specified address. If execCallbacks is true, registered callbacks may be invoked on the write.
requirements: No alignment constraints; writes one byte at addr.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setConcreteRegisterValue
functions.signature: void triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setConcreteRegisterValue(const triton::arch::Register& reg, const triton::uint512& value, bool execCallbacks = true)
functions.description: Sets the concrete value of the specified register. Only the low bits of value up to the register's size are written. If execCallbacks is true, registered callbacks may be invoked on the write.
requirements: reg must be a valid Register from this CPU model.
value must contain at least reg.size bits; higher bits are ignored.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setThumb
functions.description: Sets the CPU Thumb state flag. For x86 this has no architectural effect; provided for API uniformity.
requirements: state is a boolean flag.
Setting Thumb state on x86 likely has no effect on disassembly/semantics; exact behavior is library-defined.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::setMemoryExclusiveTag
functions.description: Sets or clears the exclusive tag on the specified memory region, used by the memory exclusivity mechanism (e.g., LL/SC).
requirements: mem must describe a valid memory region with a defined address and size (>0).
Effect on x86 semantics is library-defined; typically for cross-arch consistency.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::isConcreteMemoryValueDefined
functions.description: Returns true if all bytes in the specified memory region have defined concrete values in the CPU's memory map.
requirements: mem must specify a valid address and size (>0).

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::isConcreteMemoryValueDefined
functions.description: Returns true if all bytes in [baseAddr, baseAddr + size) have defined concrete values.
requirements: size specifies the number of bytes to test; default is 1.
Behavior for size == 0 is unspecified.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::clearConcreteMemoryValue
functions.description: Clears concrete values for the specified memory region, marking those bytes as undefined in the CPU's memory map.
requirements: mem must specify a valid address and size (>0).

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Cpu::clearConcreteMemoryValue
functions.description: Clears concrete values for the specified range [baseAddr, baseAddr + size), marking those bytes as undefined.
requirements: size specifies the number of bytes to clear; default is 1.
Behavior for size == 0 is unspecified.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Semantics::x86Semantics
functions.signature: triton::arch::x86::x86Semantics::x86Semantics(triton::arch::Architecture* architecture, triton::engines::symbolic::SymbolicEngine* symbolicEngine, triton::engines::taint::TaintEngine* taintEngine, const triton::modes::SharedModes& modes, const triton::ast::SharedAstContext& astCtxt)
functions.description: Constructor for the x86Semantics engine. It wires the semantics implementation to the provided Architecture, SymbolicEngine, TaintEngine, active Modes, and AST context so that x86 instruction semantics can be built. Typical usage: construct once per Architecture/analysis context, then call buildSemantics() for each decoded instruction. Internal members are initialized from the provided parameters. Specific initialization side effects are not documented here.
requirements: architecture must be a valid pointer to an initialized triton::arch::Architecture compatible with x86 (inferred from class purpose; exact validation behavior not documented).
symbolicEngine must be a valid pointer to an initialized triton::engines::symbolic::SymbolicEngine (inferred).
taintEngine must be a valid pointer to an initialized triton::engines::taint::TaintEngine (inferred).
modes must reference a valid triton::modes::SharedModes instance; required to reflect engine configuration (inferred).
astCtxt must reference a valid triton::ast::SharedAstContext used to create/manipulate AST nodes for symbolic semantics (inferred).
Thread-safety and ownership semantics are unknown; callers should ensure lifetime of provided objects outlives the x86Semantics instance (inferred).

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Semantics::buildSemantics
functions.description: Builds the symbolic/taint semantics of the provided x86 instruction. On success, returns triton::arch::NO_FAULT; otherwise returns an exception code indicating the kind of fault encountered. Expected usage: pass a decoded and architecture-bound Instruction; after the call, the instruction will have associated semantics expressions and updated flags/state as appropriate.
requirements: inst must reference a decoded and initialized triton::arch::Instruction representing an x86 instruction (partially inferred; header comment states it builds semantics of the instruction).
The x86Semantics object must have been constructed with valid Architecture, SymbolicEngine, TaintEngine, Modes, and AST context; behavior is undefined otherwise (inferred from constructor).
Callers must check the return value: triton::arch::NO_FAULT indicates success; any other triton::arch::exception_e value indicates a fault (explicitly documented).
Instruction’s architecture should match x86; cross-architecture use is unsupported (inferred from class scope and purpose).
Function may modify inst by attaching semantics and updating status/flags; callers should not assume inst remains unchanged (inferred).

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Specifications::x86Specifications
functions.description: Constructor that initializes x86/x86_64 architecture specifications used by Triton. It sets up internal mappings (e.g., register specifications) for the selected architecture. Typical usage: construct once for the intended x86 variant (32-bit or 64-bit) and then use the instance to perform Capstone-to-Triton conversions.
requirements: The architecture_e value must denote a supported x86 family architecture (e.g., 32-bit or 64-bit); other architectures are not valid for this class.
The instance must be successfully constructed before calling any of its conversion methods.
Thread-safety of the instance is unknown; if used across threads, external synchronization may be required.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Specifications::capstoneRegisterToTritonRegister
functions.description: Converts a Capstone x86 register identifier to the corresponding Triton register enum. Use this when translating registers reported by Capstone into Triton’s internal register identifiers.
requirements: The x86Specifications instance must be constructed for the target x86 architecture before use.
Parameter id must be a valid Capstone x86 register identifier for the same architecture as the instance.
Behavior for unknown/unsupported ids is not documented; callers should verify the returned register_e value before use.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Specifications::capstoneInstructionToTritonInstruction
functions.description: Converts a Capstone x86 instruction identifier to the corresponding Triton instruction identifier (as defined by Triton’s x86 instruction enumeration). Useful for mapping Capstone decode results to Triton’s instruction IDs.
requirements: The x86Specifications instance must be constructed for the target x86 architecture before use.
Parameter id must be a valid Capstone x86 instruction identifier.
Behavior for unknown/unsupported ids is not documented; callers should validate the returned Triton instruction ID before use.

functions.name: triton::arch::x86::x86Specifications::capstonePrefixToTritonPrefix
functions.description: Converts a Capstone x86 instruction prefix identifier to the corresponding Triton x86 prefix enum. Use this to translate Capstone-reported prefixes (e.g., segment overrides, operand-size/address-size) into Triton’s prefix representation.
requirements: The x86Specifications instance must be constructed for the target x86 architecture before use.
Parameter id must be a valid Capstone x86 prefix identifier.
Behavior for unknown/unsupported ids is not documented; callers should validate the returned prefix_e value before use.
